The Ethiopian Kebra Nagast traces Solomonic royal descent through Shem, establishing an unbroken claimed lineage from Adam to the 20th-century Ethiopian monarchy
Medieval European royal genealogies systematically claimed descent from Japheth, connecting ruling houses to the Genesis Table of Nations
The Abrahamic lineage is traced in Genesis, 1 Chronicles, and Luke through ten named generations from Shem to Abraham, with consistent names across three independent texts
The Book of Jubilees assigns specific territorial boundaries to Shem, Ham, and Japheth with geographic coordinates and landmarks
Josephus (Antiquities I.6, c. 94 CE) identifies Genesis 10 names with specific nations known in his era, providing the oldest surviving systematic key
Genesis 10 names 70 descendants of Noah and assigns them to specific territories, constituting the oldest surviving attempt at a comprehensive genealogy of nations
The Rockefeller Foundation's General Education Board, established 1902, stated its intent to shape American education and explicitly described producing compliant workers
The Smithsonian Institution received a congressional charter (1846) granting it unique custody over natural and cultural artifacts with no external audit requirement for disposals
Building Codes across multiple U.S. and European cities reveal ground-floor windows and doorways partially or fully below current street grade, consistent with a burial event
MKUltra was a real CIA program conducting illegal human experiments on unwitting subjects, documented by the agency's own surviving files
Operation Paperclip brought over 1,600 German scientists into U.S. government service after WWII, with war-crime records officially scrubbed
The U.S. Federal Reserve System was created by an act of Congress signed December 23, 1913, delegating currency issuance to a privately structured central bank
Major U.S. newspapers published hundreds of reports of oversized human skeletal remains between 1840 and 1920
The Gregorian calendar reform of 1582 removed 10 days from the calendar by papal decree; adoption took over 300 years across nations
"Tartary" or "Grande Tartarie" appears as a named sovereign territory on European maps continuously from the 16th century through the mid-19th century, then vanishes
Between 1854 and 1929, an estimated 250,000 children were transported from Eastern U.S. cities to the Midwest and West on "orphan trains" — many were not orphans
The 1611 King James Bible contained 80 books; modern editions contain 66
The Tetragrammaton (YHWH) appears approximately 6,800 times in the oldest complete Hebrew manuscript, but zero times in the King James Version
Within living memory of the events, the U.S. Congress legally acknowledged that the 1811–12 New Madrid earthquakes materially destroyed land — severe enough to warrant wholesale land replacement
Mercator's 1595 polar map cites a named source text (Inventio Fortunata) of which no copy survives anywhere

digs.title: Anomalous Fires
digs.question: The question: what do official investigation records, satellite imagery, and insurance data actually establish about burn patterns, material survival, and response timelines in recent high-loss fires (Lahaina 2023, Paradise 2018, and comparable events)?

digs.title: Book Removal
digs.question: The question: which books were present in the 1611 King James Bible that are absent from modern editions, and what is the documented history of their removal?

digs.title: Buried Architecture
digs.question: The question: what do surviving buildings, underground districts, and municipal records show about cities whose original ground floors now sit below current street grade?

digs.title: Calendar Reform
digs.question: The question: what do the primary documents show about how, when, and by whose authority the Western calendar was changed — and what dating discrepancies result from the staggered adoption?

digs.title: Civilization Resets
digs.question: The question: what does the physical, geological, and documentary record show about catastrophic discontinuities in the built environment and written record — events after which the prior state of civilization appears to reset, degrade, or vanish?

digs.title: Education System
digs.question: The question: what do the foundational documents and institutional records show about who designed the modern American public education system, what they stated their goals to be, and how those goals map to the system's actual structure?

digs.title: Giant Skeleton Reports
digs.question: The question: what do surviving 19th and early 20th century newspaper accounts actually say about oversized human skeletal remains — how many reports exist, what do they specifically claim, and what became of the reported remains?

digs.title: Institutional Capture
digs.question: The question: what do official records show about documented cases where government agencies or state-adjacent institutions altered records, concealed programs, or operated without the oversight their charters promised?

digs.title: Lineage of Nations
digs.question: The question: what do the oldest surviving genealogical texts — Genesis 5, Genesis 10 (the Table of Nations), 1 Chronicles 1, the Book of Jubilees, and Josephus's Antiquities — actually record about the descent of peoples from a common origin, and how do the names and territorial assignments in those texts map to historically attested nations and geographies?

digs.title: Map Chronology
digs.question: The question: what does the dated sequence of surviving maps actually show about how the depicted world changed — and when, and in whose hands?

digs.title: Monetary System
digs.question: The question: what do the foundational statutes and institutional records show about how the U.S. monetary system was structured, restructured, and by whose authority?

digs.title: The Name Erasure
digs.question: The question: how many times does the divine name (YHWH / יהוה) appear in the oldest Hebrew manuscripts, and what exactly was it replaced with in major English translations — when, by whom, and under what stated rationale?

digs.title: New Madrid, 1811–1812
digs.question: The question: what does the surviving physical and administrative record actually establish about the scale and nature of the New Madrid events — as distinct from both the modern textbook account and any interpretive frame?

digs.title: Orphan Trains
digs.question: The question: what do the institutional and survivor records actually establish about the scale, mechanics, and consent conditions of the orphan train movement (1854–1929)?

digs.title: Tartaria Cartography
digs.question: The question: what does the dated sequence of European maps and encyclopedias show about how "Tartary" was depicted, described, and eventually dropped from the cartographic and reference record?
